summary:
# BOOK NOTES (5 books in prompt)

## BOOK 1: Tinman (Tom Gallon, 1907)
**Narrator:** Charles Avaline, "Tinman", the ex-convict writing his memoir.
**Early life:** Orphan, dreamy, wants to be an artist. Guardian: Jervis Fanshawe (manager at Patton & Co., Bloomsbury house, sinister, long nose, thin face, chin cut, white stops on desk, paper-knife). Fanshawe's friend Gavin Hockley (big, swaggering, stick, dogcart, grin, moustache, drinks, blackmails Fanshawe over debts). Fanshawe owes Hockley money; Hockley threatens to "talk."
**Hammerstone Market:** Charles stays at the *George* inn. Meets Barbara Patton (18, daughter of old Patton, sings, "Prince Charlie" note) in woods. Hockley lies in grass, mocks him. Fanshawe in pool; ruined easel (muddy heel). Dinner at Patton's: doctor's story of a plotted murder; Lucas Savell (good-humoured cousin) engaged to Barbara by Patton's toast. Charles strikes Hockley on terrace over insult to Barbara; Hockley falls down steps, claims he slipped. Fanshawe: "Strike him dead."
**Card game:** Charles loses ~£30 to Hockley, gives IOU, Fanshawe shows nothing; Hockley: "Lucky at cards, unlucky in love."
**Supper, wedding day:** Hockley insults Barbara; Charles seizes his throat; accused of murderous attack. Fanshawe takes Charles to Patton's house. Barbara's note: "Because I love you and trust you... my poor Prince Charlie..." Charles keeps silence.
**Lincoln's Inn Fields:** Charles goes to Hockley's rooms (no weapons, takes a sword off wall), says "take back the lie"; Hockley with poker; Charles strikes him twice; Hockley dies. Fanshawe finds him on stairs.
**Fanshawe's confession:** Had engineered it; was in debt to Patton & Co.; hated Charles's youth.
**Trial:** Guilty. Judge sentences death; commuted to penal servitude for life ("on account of youth"). Prisoner number **145**. Twenty years. Barbara visits condemned cell (dream visions of wood); she promises silence; she later leaves for abroad, stepfather name etc.
**Release:** Fanshawe meets him at prison gates, reminds him he's "Charlie." Fanshawe was also jailed for seven years (forgery). Moggs (girl at lodging near river, 15-16). Fanshawe reveals Barbara died at sea, daughter (also named Barbara, age ~16-18) lives at Hammerstone; Lucas Savell weak, drinking; Murray Olivant holds business; Arnold Millard (half-brother of Olivant, painter, loves new Barbara).
**Tinman:** Charles renamed "Tinman" by Olivant; servant at Patton house. Sees ghost/face at window. Barbara knows he is a gentleman. Olivant (Murray) wants new Barbara; Dawkins (smiling). Olivant kidnaps? Olivant fights Tinman on stairs; "I killed a man once." Tinman sends Barbara to meet Arnold; Olivant intercepts with forged note; Barbara taken to London by Dawkins. Olivant fakes voyage to Mediterranean; Charles and Fanshawe's Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms. Olivant found stabbed in his rooms (by Arnold? or Fanshawe), Fanshawe confesses to Charles; Fanshawe takes steamer ticket and dies in wreck of SS *Eaglet* (fog off Ushant; survivor Henry Howard).
**Ending:** Charles (Tinman) reappears at Hammerstone Market, hospitalised earlier; Barbara (Patton daughter) marries Arnold Millard. Charles and Barbara (the elder, now "Mrs. Avaline," who had been alive) reunite; she takes his name. Lucas Savell has stroke, dies ~three months after. Charles's narration ends with "Eternal".

Key names: Charles Avaline (No. 145, Tinman), Jervis Fanshawe, Gavin Hockley, Barbara Patton (elder) / Barbara Savell (new Barbara), Lucas Savell, Patton, Murray Olivant, Dawkins, Arnold Millard, Moggs, Mrs. Briscoe no. Mrs. Rolfe no. Warden Forest no.

## BOOK 2: Just a Girl (Charles Garvice, 1895)
**Setting:** Three Star Camp, Australian gold camp; Eldorado Saloon (Dan MacGrath); Varley Howard (gambler, languid, tall hat, won the infant by cards); Bill the postman; Mother Melinda; Taffy (Welsh giant); the Penman (school-master); Dog's Ear (rival camp); Esmeralda (foundling, named at saloon). Doctor, Smifkens (baronet).
**Esmeralda** grows up loved by camp; teach by Penman; rides, shoots. Meets **Lord Norman Druce** (fair, blue eyes, Oakfield manor, cousin of Lord Trafford), shot in leg at Dog's Ear; she rescues him. Norman declares love; she refuses.
**Mr. Pinchook** (solicitor) reveals Esmeralda is granddaughter of Gordon Chetwynde (£2 million). She goes to England with Pinchook; Lady Wyndover (guardian, flaxen hair, carmine lips) in Grosvenor Square; Madame Cerise dressmaker; Barker maid.
**London:** Lady Blankyre's party; Lord Selvaine (small, grey, sharp) introduces Lord Trafford (Marquis, eldest son of Duke of Belfayre). Lady Ada Lancing (fair, blue eyes, Scotch peer's daughter; Trafford's old love, pining). Trafford's family in debt; Selvaine plots marriage with heiress. Trafford proposes at Shirley/Surrey drive; Esmeralda accepts.
**Belfayre:** Duke (courtly, benign, son Trafford's father), Lilias Selvaine (niece, 19, small, mistress of house), Helby (steward), Norman's love for Lilias. Duke dies in sleep; Esmeralda kisses him.
**Wedding:** Church, bishop, Lord Ffoulkes best man; Lord Blankyre "gives her away." Ada as bridesmaid. Wedding night: Esmeralda learns Trafford married for money, overhears Ada. Fight. Esmeralda leaves Belfayre at night; Trafford finds Norman's letter (passed via Ada), believes Esmeralda adulterous; they separate.
**Australia:** Esmeralda returns to Three Star; Varley and boys greet her; Trafford follows, duels Varley at Raven Claim (Esmeralda shot in shoulder while protecting Trafford; survives). Norman arrives; Trafford reconciled with Norman (Ada's letter revealed). Esmeralda and Trafford reunited, love confessed.
**Final:** Lilias and Norman marry; Varley visits England. Lady Ada on Continent.

## BOOK 3: Only One Love; or, Who Was the Heir? (Charles Garvice)
**Opening:** Forest of Warden; young man (Jack Newcombe, "the Savage") lost, stays at woodman Gideon Rolfe's hut. Gideon's daughter **Una** (about 21, bronze-gold hair, brown eyes, lady-like, raised in wood). Wife **Martha Rolfe**; dog Dick. Gideon refuses to shake hands with Jack; warns Una off.
**Squire Redmond Maynard** of Hazelwell; son **Ulick** left home two years earlier after accusation over **Janet Todd** (Eli Todd's daughter). Hound **Bersak**. Irene Carstone (ward, now married to **Warren Courtly** of Anselm Manor; Random horse painting).
**Eli Todd**, stud manager; Honeysuckle mare's foal; Janet ran away with Warren Courtly (not Ulick).
**Felix Hoffman**: Feltham blackmailer; writes to Irene; Janet lives at Mrs. Hoffman's as "Mrs. Warren."
**The Saint**: grey racehorse Ulick buys from Fred May; wins Pastures Handicap and Coronation Cup over Vulture.
**Warren's death**: Jumps Glen church wall dared by Ulick; killed on gravestone. Ulick and Irene marry; Janet returns to Eli; son born.
**Ending:** Squire reconciled; family harmony.

## BOOK 4: Won at Last; or, Mrs. Briscoe's Nephews (Agnes Giberne)
**Narrator:** Mother (Marion Hazel), wife of Robert Hazel (poor London clerk). Children: **Jack** (eldest, slow but kind, loves Maimie), **Cherry** (twin of Cress, loyal, pretty in quiet way), **Cresswell "Cress"** (handsome, selfish, clever), **Owen** (steady, north of England), **Fred** (training ship), **Bob, Edmund/Ted** (youngest). Aunt **Elizabeth Briscoe** of "The Gables" (rich widow, will heir: Robert).
**Maimie Browne** (Mary, "Maimie"; 14→17) arrives unannounced, stepdaughter of **Churton Hazel** (Robert's brother, in Canada/America, loud, selfish). Maimie nursed through measles/pneumonia; teaches boys, helps Jack with spelling and figures.
**Churton** returns; takes Maimie to The Gables; Aunt Briscoe changes will to Churton; Maimie reveals Churton's trick to take inheritance. Will ultimately reverts: "The Gables" and money to Robert; £1000 to Jack. Maimie marries Jack; Cress goes to India; Churton sent letter from South Africa.

## BOOK 5: The Runaways (Nat Gould, 1900s)
**Setting:** Hazelwell Hall; Redmond Maynard (squire), son Ulick Maynard (accused, left home two years earlier). Irene Carstone (ward, married Warren Courtly of Anselm Manor). Eli Todd (stud), daughter Janet Todd (ran off). Bersak (wolfhound). Random (bay hunter; Irene's painting). Honeysuckle's foal (New Year's Eve, ~midnight). Felix Hoffman (blackmailer, Feltham, Mrs. Hoffman). Fred May (trainer, Stanton House, Newmarket). The Saint (grey, "curiosity," olive green colours, Ben Sprig jockey). Dr. Harding; James Bard (vet at Helton).
**Events:** Night of Ulick's anniversary; Irene at Hazelwell. Ulick secretly visits Eli; learns Janet ran off the same night with Warren. Ulick buys the Saint for 200 guineas. Ulick sees Janet at Feltham; Warren arrives; Janet and Ulick conceal Ulick. Warren's gambling; sells Holme Farm for £10,000. Felix extorts Warren; Irene visits Janet, learns all. Pastures Handicap (Kempton) and Coronation Cup (Epsom, Derby week): the Saint beats Vulture by short head. Squire and Ulick reconcile at Walton Hotel. Hunt at Helton: Warren dares Ulick to jump Glen church wall; Warren's grey falls, Warren killed (neck broken). Janet returns to Eli. Ulick and Irene marry; son born.
